key_insight: A realistic SLM noise model shows that universal single- and two-qubit photonic gates on OAM qubits can still achieve high simulated fidelity, enabling software-defined quantum operations with hardware-informed accuracy.
engineering_relevance: This work provides a practical design and benchmarking framework for using transmissive spatial light modulators as reconfigurable quantum hardware for photonic information processing.
method: Simulated OAM-encoded qubits on a 512×512 grid using Laguerre-Gaussian beams and phase holography.
Built a three-part noise model from the HOLOEYE LC 2012 datasheet: 8-bit quantisation, twisted-nematic electronic/thermal noise, and phase-wrap clipping error.
Evaluated universal gates {X, Y, Z, S, T, H} and entangling gates {CNOT, CZ, SWAP}, plus Bell-state preparation via H-CNOT.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports gate fidelities of 0.9914–0.9936, Bell-state fidelity of 0.9914, and a benchmark comparison against six experiments spanning 78%–99.6% fidelity.
watch_item: The results are simulation-based and depend on datasheet-derived noise assumptions, so real-device performance may vary with alignment, calibration, and wavelength drift.
paper_title: Simulating Universal Quantum Gate Sets on Photonic OAM Qubits: Single-Qubit and Multi-Qubit Operations via Spatial Light Modulator Phase Holography
